**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What the document says.** Termination is governed by § 6. Subsection (a) gives *either* party a convenience right on 15 days' notice, but only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." Subsection (b) is a for-cause right (uncured material breach, 15 days). Section 2 makes the Agreement evergreen, running "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6."

**Why it fails the fallback.** The net effect is that once an SOW is signed, Clear Capital has no convenience exit at all — only breach termination — for the full duration of the engagement, which on a time-and-materials consulting agreement can easily exceed 12 months. The playbook's walk-away line is "no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term," and the detection guidance treats absence of a customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months as a missing-behaviour deviation. The fallback (60–90 days' notice, fee capped at 3 months) is not met either, because no customer convenience right exists mid-SOW at any notice period.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** A single appended sentence to § 6(a) adding the preferred 30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, with payment for Services performed through the effective date and refund of prepaid amounts. This is the smallest edit reaching the preferred position and leaves the existing sentence untouched.

**Deliberately not flagged.** Contractor's 15-day convenience right looks short against the 90-day walk-away threshold, but it is exercisable only when no SOW is outstanding, so it cannot be used to abandon us mid-engagement — the mischief the rule targets. I noted it in the rationale rather than redlining it, to keep the ask narrow and avoid spending negotiating capital on a right that carries no practical risk.
